newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on late speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on late speculation.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 320 basis points at 25.80 percent on Friday due to late speculation, after rates fluctuated widely at moderate trade during the session, dealers said.
"It was speculation that kept levels so low. Paper is concentrated in few hands, and they are taking advantage of that," said a trader.
Traders also said that relative stability in the foreign exchange market also helped secondary rates to fall.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed earlier 1.1 centavos weaker at 7.7280/7.7340 per dollar.
Despite relative calm in the foreign exchange market, traders said they expected primary Cetes rates to rise again at next week's auction.
"We expect another hike to bolster the peso, although the extent will depend on how the peso fares on Monday and Tuesday," said another trader.
The bellwether 28-day Cetes rate rose to 25.90 percent at the last auction.
The Cetes 28-day rate fell 75 basis points to 27.0 percent, and 91-day rates closed off 100 basis points at 27.75 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 95 basis points at 29.0 percent.
Traders said liquidity shortfalls during the session were eased by the government spending an estimated 2 billion pesos.
Total credit maturities for Monday are estimated at 4.065 billion pesos.
